# Spec: monorepo-spec-roots
<!-- Generated by /hef.spec -->
<!-- Date: 2026-11-05 -->
<!-- Source: issue #172; maintainer decisions in the #172 comment of 2026-11-05 -->

## Overview

One git repository can hold several apps, each with its own `.specify/` (a *spec root*): `backend/.specify/`,
`frontend/.specify/`. Hefesto finds the spec root the way git finds `.git`, instead of assuming the repository
top. A board item names the app that owns it, and the pipeline (the helper, the guards, the launcher, the ledger
and the board) works in that app's folder. A repository with no `spec_roots` setting behaves as it does today.

## Terms

- **Spec root**: a folder holding a `.specify/` directory. The *top spec root* is the repository top's own.
- **App**: a named spec root declared in `.claude/project-status.json` as `"spec_roots": {"<name>": "<folder>"}`.
  The folder is relative to the repository top.
- **Owning root** of an item: the app named in the item's ledger entry (`spec_root`), or the repository top when
  none is named.
- **Discovery**: starting at a path, take the nearest ancestor (the path itself included) that contains a
  `.specify/` directory. Stop at the repository top, and never go above it. If none is found, the starting
  folder is used, as today.

## User Scenarios

### US1: The helper works from an app folder [P1]
- **Given** a repository with `backend/.specify/specs/audit-log/` and the branch `feature/audit-log`
- **When** `speckit-helper.sh spec` runs from `backend/` or from `backend/internal/store/`
- **Then** it prints `backend/.specify/specs/audit-log/spec.md`
- **Edge:** run from the repository top with no top `.specify/specs/audit-log/`, it fails as today ("Run
  /hef.spec first") and names the spec roots that hold the feature.
- **Error:** `plan-phase-start` from `backend/internal/` writes the marker in `backend/.specify/`. It never
  creates `backend/internal/.specify/`.

### US2: The constitution is inherited [P1]
- **Given** a top `.specify/memory/constitution.md` and `backend/.specify/memory/constitution.md`
- **When** `speckit-helper.sh constitution` runs from `backend/`
- **Then** it prints the top constitution under a heading that marks it inherited, then the app's
- **Edge:** the app has no constitution of its own, so the top one is printed alone, marked inherited.
- **Error:** neither exists, so it fails as today. In a single-root repository the output is byte-identical to
  today's.

### US3: The guards follow the spec root [P1]
- **Given** the implement marker at `backend/.specify/.implement-in-progress`
- **When** an edit removes an assertion from `backend/store_test.go`, and the session's cwd is the repository
  top, `backend/`, or `frontend/`
- **Then** `implement-phase-test-guard.sh` blocks it. The guard is armed when the spec root found from the cwd
  or the one found from the edited file holds the marker.
- **Edge:** with the session in `backend/`, the plan marker in `backend/.specify/` blocks a write to
  `frontend/src/app.tsx` and allows one to `backend/.specify/specs/x/plan.md`. From the top or `frontend/`,
  neither side's root holds the marker, so that write is not blocked. A planner runs in its app folder
  (FR-009, FR-014), and the guards read no config.
- **Error:** with no marker in either spec root, nothing is blocked, as today.

### US4: A board item is owned by one app [P1]
- **Given** `spec_roots` = `{"backend": "backend", "frontend": "frontend"}` and item BAT-7, whose body has the line
  `app: backend`
- **When** the orchestrator registers or launches BAT-7
- **Then** the ledger entry records `spec_root: "backend"`. The plan and implement sessions run with cwd =
  `<worktree>/backend`. The planner's edit rules name `backend/.specify/**` only. The recorded `spec_dir` is
  `backend/.specify/specs/<name>`, relative to the worktree.
- **Edge:** the item has no `app:` line while `spec_roots` is declared. The orchestrator asks one form
  ("Which app owns BAT-7?", one option per app plus "the repository root") and records the answer.
- **Error:** `app: payments` when `payments` is not declared is refused with the declared names. An item with no
  launch claim is not launched in a guessed folder.

### US5: A single-app repository does not change [P1]
- **Given** no `spec_roots` key
- **When** any stage runs
- **Then** the cwd, the planner's allowlist, the prompts and the guards' decisions are the same as in 9.2.0. The
  one difference is that a new `spec_dir` is recorded relative to the worktree (`.specify/specs/<name>`).
- **Edge:** an entry written before 9.3.0 with an absolute `spec_dir` still unblocks, launches and answers
  `ledger questions`.

### US6: The board reads every spec root [P2]
- **Given** `epics.specs: true` and tasks in `backend/.specify/specs/a/` and `frontend/.specify/specs/b/`
- **When** `status-board.sh` prints epics
- **Then** both are listed, labelled `backend/a` and `frontend/b`
- **Edge:** a declared app folder with no `.specify/specs/` adds no line and no error.

### US7: Gates run in the app folder, repository checks run once [P2]
- **Given** an item owned by `backend`
- **When** `/hef.quality` or `/hef.verify` runs
- **Then** tests, lint and types use the commands detected in `backend/`. Secrets, CI and workflow files, and a
  root `Makefile` are checked once from the repository top.

### US8: Interactive lanes work in the app folder [P2]
- **Given** an interactive stage lane and an item owned by `backend`
- **When** `session-launch.sh --prepare` prepares it
- **Then** it prints an extra line, `app: <worktree>/backend`, and the stage text tells the lane to run every
  command from that folder. An item with no owning app prints the same lines as today.

## Functional Requirements

### Must have

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-001 | A new library, `hooks/spec-root-lib.sh`, gives `spec_root_find <path>`. It returns the nearest ancestor of `<path>` holding `.specify/`, stops at the git top (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, inclusive), and prints the starting folder when none is found. A path outside any git repository is treated as its own top. | P1 | US1 |
| FR-002 | `speckit-helper.sh` resolves the spec root once, from its cwd, and runs every `.specify/...` lookup there: artifacts, specs, checklists, phase markers, mutation-score, req-coverage. `check-specify-dir` (used by `/hef.init`) stays literal to the cwd, so `/hef.init` in an app folder creates that app's `.specify/`. | P1 | US1 |
| FR-003 | When an artifact is missing, the helper's message names the top and every declared app that holds `.specify/specs/<branch>/` (no tree walk), so "run /hef.spec first" is never the only hint when the spec lives in an app. | P1 | US1 |
| FR-004 | `constitution` prints the top constitution, marked inherited, before the app's when the spec root is not the top. A single-root repository's output is unchanged. | P1 | US2 |
| FR-005 | `implement-phase-test-guard.sh`, `plan-phase-write-block.sh`, `spec-cite-probe.sh` and `precompact-progress.sh` resolve markers and specs through `spec_root_find`. Each guard is armed when the marker is in the spec root of the cwd or of the edited file (it fails closed: either one arms it). `spec-cite-probe.sh` scans the specs of both roots. | P1 | US3 |
| FR-006 | `spec_roots` in `project-status.json` is validated wherever it is read. Names match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$`. A folder is relative, has no `..`, and is not `.claude` or under it. A bad entry makes the reading command fail, naming the entry and the expected shape. `spec_roots` is read from the code repository's own `.claude/project-status.json`. On an external board that is the entry repository's config, never the board's. | P1 | US4 |
| FR-007 | The ledger entry gains `spec_root` (a declared name, or null for the top). It is set by `ledger.sh record <id> --spec-root <name\|.>`, where `.` is the repository top (`top` is a legal app name, never a keyword). The command refuses a name not declared in the entry's repository, and refuses once `spec_dir` is recorded (moving the owner would orphan the spec). An entry with `spec_dir` recorded and `spec_root` null (planned before `spec_roots` existed) is never undecided: its owner is derived from `spec_dir` (the longest declared folder it starts with, else `.`). An undeclared `app:` name at registration leaves no entry. Registration records the `app:` line's name, and `ledger.sh spec-roots <id>` and `list --undecided-app` feed the orchestrator's form. | P1 | US4 |
| FR-008 | An item's body may carry an `app: <name>` line, parsed like the `rfc:` line. The orchestrator records it with FR-007. When `spec_roots` is declared and the item has no line, `/hef.orchestrate` asks one form (each app, plus the repository root) and records the answer; the launcher refuses a plan launch (or an implement launch from `queued`) while `spec_root` is undecided. An undeclared name is a refusal, not a form. `/hef.ship` asks the same form when it creates the item and writes the line (`status-board.sh --add --app`). | P1 | US4 |
| FR-009 | `session-launch.sh` (headless) starts plan, implement and verify sessions with cwd = `<worktree>/<folder>` of the owning root. The planner's allowlist is `Edit(.specify/**)` plus the absolute `<worktree>/<folder>/.specify/**`. The prompts name that folder instead of "this worktree's root". A launch whose owning folder, or that folder's `.specify/`, is missing in the worktree fails, naming it and `/hef.init`. So a launched session never climbs from an app with no `.specify/` to the top's. An app folder that resolves outside the worktree (a committed symlink) is refused. | P1 | US4 |
| FR-010 | The recorded `spec_dir` is relative to the worktree (`backend/.specify/specs/x`). Every reader resolves it as `<worktree>/<spec_dir>`: `ledger.sh` block/unblock/questions/status, `ledger-lanes.sh`, the launcher's prompts. An absolute `spec_dir` from an older entry is used as is. A relative one with `..` is refused. A relative one recorded by hand on an entry with no `worktree` is read from the repository top, as 9.2.0 read it; it never resolves to `/<path>`. | P1 | US5 |
| FR-011 | With no `spec_roots` key, the launcher's cwd, allowlist and prompt text are byte-identical to 9.2.0's. | P1 | US5 |

### Should have

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-012 | `status-board.sh` epics walk the top spec root and every declared app, labelled `<app>/<feature>` when `spec_roots` is set. | P2 | US6 |
| FR-013 | `/hef.quality` and `/hef.verify` text: app checks from the owning app folder, repository-wide checks (secrets, `.github/` workflows, root `Makefile`) once from the top. `req-coverage` searches tests in the owning app folder. | P2 | US7 |
| FR-014 | `session-launch.sh --prepare` prints `app: <absolute folder>` when the owning root is an app. The interactive stage text in `/hef.orchestrate` tells the lane to `cd` there after `EnterWorktree` and to run every command from it. | P2 | US8 |
| FR-015 | A cross-app path is allowed for the owning item and named in its `tasks.md` (the plan and tasks text says so). The reviewer sees the reach. No hook enforces it. | P2 | US4 |
| FR-016 | `docs/` describe `spec_roots`, the `app:` line, discovery and constitution inheritance in one section. `CHANGELOG.md` has a 9.3.0 entry. | P2 | US4 |

### Edge cases (covered by the FRs above, tested on their own)

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-017 | Discovery never returns a folder above the git top, even when an ancestor of the repository holds a `.specify/` (a home-folder one). | P1 | US1 |
| FR-018 | A nested spec root wins over its parent (`backend/api/.specify/` beats `backend/.specify/` for a path under `backend/api/`). | P1 | US1 |
| FR-019 | A symlinked `.specify` is not followed to another repository: a `.specify` that resolves outside the git top is skipped. | P1 | US1 |

## Not in scope

- One item with specs in several apps (decided: one owning root).
- A board per app. The board stays one per repository.
- The multi-repo case (#30, `workflow.js`).
- Moving existing specs between roots.
- `workflows/workflow.js`: it already takes `projectRoot` as the folder that contains `.specify/`
  (`workflows/workflow.js:464`), so it follows an app folder unchanged.

## Success Criteria

| ID | Criterion | Validation Method |
|----|-----------|-------------------|
| SC-001 | The #172 "expected failure" fixture (a `backend/` + `frontend/` repository, `/hef.init` from `backend/`) runs spec → plan-phase markers → artifacts from `backend/` and from a subfolder of it with no root `.specify/` created | smoke part 10 (`tests/smoke-spec-roots.sh`) |
| SC-002 | Every guard FR (FR-005) has a mutant that turns the suite red: drop the file-side resolution, drop the cwd-side resolution | smoke part 10 mutants |
| SC-003 | A launcher dry run for an app-owned item shows cwd `<worktree>/backend` and the backend-only allowlist. One for a no-`spec_roots` repository matches 9.2.0's output byte for byte | smoke part 10, diffing against `tests/fixtures/launch-920.txt` (captured from the v9.2.0 tree, normalised) |
| SC-004 | The full suite passes, and so does the macOS CI job (bash 3.2) | `tests/smoke.sh`, CI |
| SC-005 | A live run on a real two-app repository: one item is planned and built in its app folder | person-run, after the release |

## Clarifications

- 2026-11-05 (maintainer, #172): one owning spec root per item, with paths in other apps allowed and listed in
  its tasks. The root constitution is inherited under each app's, as `CLAUDE.md` files nest. Tests, lint and
  types run from the app folder; repository-wide checks run once at the root.
- Decided here (best practice, no product choice): the item names its app with an `app:` line, like `rfc:`, or a
  form when the line is missing. `spec_dir` is relative to the worktree. Guards fail closed (either side's
  marker arms them). `req-coverage` searches the owning app only, since FR ids repeat across apps.
- Decided here: `spec-cite-probe.sh` scans the specs of the cwd's root and of the edited file's root, not every
  configured root as #172 proposal 5 says. FR ids repeat across apps, so a test in `frontend/` checked against
  `backend/`'s specs would match the wrong requirement. The guards also read no config.
